title: Mnemosyne, Incarna of Memory
summary: The spirit who remembers the whole Near Umbra.

claims.text: Mnemosyne keeps no single home; the Incarna roams the whole Near Umbra, taking in all it holds, and knows every corner, hidden niche and lost realm.
Mnemosyne forgets nothing except by choice. A thing Mnemosyne chooses to forget sees its spiritual image drift toward the Abyss, where it may be lost for good.
Mokole are tied to Mnemosyne through Mnesis and the Mnetics.

title: Fera of Mesoamerica
summary: The shapeshifters of the Maya, Aztec and Inca lands before the Garou came.

claims.text: Ananasi worked among the Maya, quietly fostering astronomy, mathematics and writing, which are Weaver tools.

Maya expansion kept pushing into Mokole lands, and the Mokole struck back hard; seeing how the Camazotz gained power through human influence, the werejaguars looked to rising nations further north for the same.
The Fera of the region waged a hidden war for dominance in the jungles and city streets, and that endless strife helped the Garou overrun them quickly later.
The Ananasi did best of all by avoiding fights with other shapeshifters and steering human empires, urging Aztec rulers and advisers to build bigger cities and expand.

title: The Second War of Rage
summary: The Garou conquest of the New World's Fera.

claims.text: Garou stories tell of a War of Rage in which werewolves, sure that they alone kept Gaia's charge against the Weaver and the Wyrm, made war on Fera they judged to be failing their duty.
When the Garou followed European colonists to the Americas, a Second War of Rage broke out against the native Fera, alongside human genocide of those Fera's families and Kinfolk.
Ratkin in Spain laughed at a human seeking money to reach India and China by sailing west, having more urgent worries of their own about crowded cities.
